## Context / Problem

ADR 0125 puts `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` in each verifying environment's own configuration, not the repository.

Nothing enforces that. `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` is an ordinary `[verify]` key (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`, `VerifyConfig.trusted_opcert_keys`). The CI op-cert gate is the `verify-opcert` step of `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`, which runs `rebar verify-opcert` on the checked-out change. `cli()` in `src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py` calls `config.compose_config(root=args.root)` and `trusted_opcert_pairs(args.root)` (`src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py:114`), and both resolve the project layer through `_discover_project_config` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:160`), which reads the working-tree `rebar.toml`. So a change under review that adds its own key to `rebar.toml`, drops `verify.require_environment`, or sets `[tracker] dir` to an empty directory (the gate also resolves its store through `config.tracker_dir(args.root)`, `verify_opcert.py:131`, and through `show_ticket`/`current_material_fingerprint`) loosens the very gate run that checks it.

## Approach (operator decision, 2026-11-20)

The gate resolves its trust configuration from main's committed `rebar.toml`, never from the `rebar.toml` in the change under review.

Implement this in-process in `rebar verify-opcert`, so it holds under any CI provider or none:

- New module `src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py` with `gate_config(root) -> (Config, source, OperationSnapshot)`. It composes the `load_config` layers (user, project, env, `-c`), but the project layer is the config committed at the base ref (`git show <ref>:<path>`). Discovery: nearest `rebar.toml`, else `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.rebar]`, from the project root up to the top level. `$REBAR_CONFIG` is ignored (it could name a working-tree file), so `_discover_project_config` is not reused. The working-tree project config is never read.
- Base ref: `refs/remotes/origin/main` only, the ref attested gates already treat as reviewed main (`rebar.llm.gate_source.DEFAULT_REF`, `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:71`). Failure handling, every arm:
  - a remote exists but `origin/main` does not resolve: `ConfigError`, exit 2, naming the `git fetch` that fixes it;
  - `ls-tree` fails, `git show` of a listed path fails (for example a blobless clone cannot fetch the blob), or the TOML does not parse: `ConfigError`, exit 2;
  - the path is absent at the ref (decided by `git ls-tree --full-tree --name-only <ref> -- <path>`, which reads trees only): fall through to the next candidate, then to an empty project layer;
  - `git remote` exits non-zero (not a repository, safe.directory refusal): `ConfigError`, exit 2;
  - no remote at all (`git remote` succeeds and prints nothing): no reviewed branch and no change under review, so the working-tree configuration is kept.
- `cli()` takes every gate value (`require_environment`, `opcert_enforce_since`, `trusted_opcert_keys`) from the `gate_config` result and calls neither `compose_config` nor `trusted_opcert_pairs(args.root)`; `trusted_opcert_pairs` is split so the gate parses the list it holds (`opcert_pairs(entries)`). It prints the trust source to stderr.
- The same configuration is returned as an `OperationSnapshot` (`src/rebar/_operation_config.py:81`) and bound for the run with `bind_operation_snapshot`. That covers only snapshot-aware readers — `config.tracker_dir` (`src/rebar/config.py:152`) and `_config_value` — so the store `show_ticket` and the material recomputation walk is main's `tracker.dir`. `load_config`/`compose_config` ignore the snapshot, so two working-tree reads remain in a live `show_ticket` and each is handled:
  - read-time sync: `ensure_fresh` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:230`) calls `_sync_disabled` → `compose_config`, so the change's `sync.pull` would decide whether the store reconverges, and a raising read escapes `show_ticket` and drops the ticket from scope. The gate runs under `local_read_context()` (`reads.py:145`), which returns before that lookup: the gate verifies the store as mounted (the CI step fetches and mounts `tickets` explicitly).
  - the advisory cross-session warning toggle (`_commands/cross_session.py:46`); `_lib_warn.emit_cross_session_warning` swallows every error and it cannot change the verdict.
  A test runs the gate in-process from the fixture repo (cwd and `REBAR_ROOT`), defeats the 60 s freshness throttle, and makes every working-tree project-config discovery raise `AssertionError` (not `ConfigError`, which `_sync_disabled` would swallow); it still requires main's `untrusted` verdict. Without `local_read_context()` it fails (0 tickets in scope, exit 0).
- `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`: the `verify-opcert` step fetches `refs/heads/main` into `refs/remotes/origin/main` (blobless, after the pack measurement) before running the gate.
- Docs: the `verify-opcert` parser description (regenerated `src/rebar/_cli/help/*.txt` and `docs/cli-reference.md`), `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/manifest-signing.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md` (the new exit-2 cases), and `infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md` (an enforcement flip takes effect after it merges, not in its own gate run).

Out of scope: the environment layer stays (ADR 0125); keeping it, the gate's code and the workflow file out of the change's reach is the CI lane's job. The sibling `verify-identity` gate is not changed.

No config key, env var or flag is added: the base ref is fixed at `origin/main`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py` (new)
- `src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py`
- `src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py`
- `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/verify.py`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/verify-opcert.txt`, `docs/cli-reference.md`
- `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/manifest-signing.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md`, `infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md`
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_gate_config.py` (new)

## Testing

`tests/unit/test_opcert_gate_config.py`, with a local bare repo as `origin`, covers: the end-to-end attack (exit 1 `untrusted` before merge, exit 0 after, and exit 0 on the old gate), an in-process run with working-tree config reads forced to raise, an unfetchable blob in a blobless clone, dirty and committed change configs ignored, `require_environment` not droppable, the environment trust list still applied, `pyproject.toml [tool.rebar]` on main, a redirected `tracker.dir`, a missing `origin/main` (exit 2 naming `git fetch origin`), and a remote-less checkout. The existing remote-less `tests/unit/test_verify_opcert*.py` fixtures pass unchanged. Full `make verify` before push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The CI op-cert gate reads `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` from main's committed `rebar.toml`, not the change's: `.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml` fetches `origin/main` before `rebar verify-opcert`, and `gate_config` reads the project layer at that ref (`test_gate_config_ignores_the_working_tree_project_config`).
- [x] A change that adds a key to `rebar.toml` does not widen the trust list its own gate run uses: `test_change_adding_its_own_key_does_not_widen_its_gate_run` passes, and fails against the pre-fix `verify_opcert.py`.
- [x] The gate run reaches main's verdict with every working-tree project-config read raising: `test_gate_run_never_needs_the_working_tree_project_config` passes.
- [x] An unfetchable committed `rebar.toml` fails closed: `test_unfetchable_blob_on_main_fails_closed` passes.
- [x] A change setting `[tracker] dir` cannot redirect the store the gate walks: `test_change_cannot_redirect_the_store_it_walks` passes.
- [x] No config key, env var or flag is added: `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0 and `git diff origin/main -- src/rebar/_config_schema.py` is empty.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_gate_config.py tests/unit/test_verify_opcert.py tests/unit/test_verify_opcert_ac_coverage.py` passes.
